reason: Jung in his own voice: 'synchronicity is its para-psychological equivalent' (of the unus mundus), and the synchronistic principle 'postulates a unitary aspect of being which can very well be described as the unus mundus.'

'Mandala symbolism is the psychological equivalent of the unus mundus' — mandala as the symbol/equivalent of the unus mundus, direction correct; though cast as a conditional, Jung affirms both halves in the same passage.
Reversed. The paragraph says of Leo: 'on the one hand he is an allegory of the devil' — the lion symbolizes the devil, not the devil the lion.
The text says 'Mercurius corresponds to the Holy Ghost as well as to the Anthropos' — a correspondence, not an identity; 'identical-to' is identity overreach.
Reversed. The vessel is the 'matrix or uterus from which the filius philosophorum, the miraculous stone, is to be born' — the vessel produces the filius, not the filius the vessel.
The paragraph says the winged youth (Sol) 'will become real only if he can unite with Luna, the mother of mortal bodies'; the monocolus appears nowhere in this paragraph.
The aqua permanens is expressly listed among the 'media of conjunction' alongside Mercurius and the green lion; the coniunctio 'occurs in — a medium.'
Jung states that the coniunctio 'corresponds to the central significance of the transference in psychotherapy'; corresponds-to is symmetric and the claim is in his own voice.
'According to its position in the quaternity, it [salt] is correlated with the feminine, lunar side' — direct assertion in Jung's expository voice.

The parallel is real (Jung frames the passage as the apotheosis of the filius regius with messianic imagery), but the supporting quote 'a splendid living likeness of our Saviour Jesus Christ' is Khunrath's quoted words about the filius Mundi Maioris, not Jung's own voice.
The paragraph says Adam 'readily lent itself as a biblical synonym for the alchemical Mercurius'; Cadmus is never mentioned — the object is a node swap.
'The quaternity of the self appears in Ezekiel's vision as the true psychological foundation of the God-concept' — Jung's own assertion; God-concept/God-image variance is negligible here.
'The sublimation of Luna ... is an unmistakable paraphrase on the one hand of the Assumption of the Virgin' — Jung's own interpretive claim, direction correct.
The quote actually reads 'salt is an arcane substance'; arsenic appears nowhere in the paragraph — the object appears to be a garbling of 'arcanum'.
The Zohar (via the Haye Sarah on Genesis 28:22) 'says that Malchuth is called the statue when she is united with Tifereth'; claim_type jung-quotes-source with the Zohar correctly named.

'This potential world is the mundus archetypus of the Schoolmen' — the potential world under discussion is Dorn's unus mundus, which the same paragraph names ('an earlier witness to the idea of the unus mundus').
'The king, is none other than gold, the king of metals' — Jung's reading of the Zosimos text, honestly cast as reported doctrine with Zosimos named.
The libido 'personifies itself in figures of heroes with solar attributes' — the hero figure carries solar symbolism; hero and sun are paired as libido symbols in Jung's own voice.

The link is real but the sentence 'It stands for the long-lasting restitution of things; indeed, it is renewal itself' continues the report of Horapollo's views ('According to Horapollo ... whose views were taken over by later writers'), so it is reported doctrine miscast as jung-asserts.
The caelum's purpose was to create 'that truth, the celestial balsam or life principle, which is identical with the God-image' — explicit identity in Jung's own psychological interpretation.
'The Mother of God represents the body' and 'the world of the body they represented by the feminine or passive principle, namely Mary' — direction correct, Jung's own interpretive assertion.
Reversed. 'She was very distinctly prefigured in the Sophia of the Old Testament' — Sophia prefigures Mary, not Mary Sophia.
'The dogmatic aspect of the evil principle is absent from the Trinity and leads a more or less awkward existence on its own as the devil' — direct assertion in Jung's voice.
'Our time contains and produces more than enough of that crude sulphur which with arsenical malignity prevents man from discovering his true self' — Jung's own symbolic application of sulphur.
'The doves are emblems of innocence and of marital love as well as of the Holy Ghost and Sapientia' — the dove as emblem of Sapientia, direction correct.
'The aim of the circulatio is the production (or rather, reproduction) of the Original Man, who was a sphere' — Original Man = Anthropos, Jung's own voice.
Reversed. 'Adam stands not only for the psyche but for its totality; he is a symbol of the self' — Adam symbolizes the Self, not the Self Adam.

The quoted sentence 'The Red Sea signifies baptism' is St. Augustine's, explicitly introduced with 'St. Augustine says'; presenting a quoted patristic source as jung-asserts is dishonest claim-typing, though Jung does endorse the baptismal-water equivalence in his framing.
The quote says 'This true man is Dorn's vir unus and at the same time the lapis Philosophorum'; fishes' eyes appear nowhere in the paragraph — object is a node swap.
Reversed. 'He [the king] represents a dominant of consciousness, such as a generally accepted principle' — Rex personifies the dominant of consciousness, not the dominant the king.
'His birth is a rebirth from the mother-wife. That is why the hero so often has two mothers' — direct assertion with examples (Heracles/Hera, Hiawatha, Buddha).

The paragraph ties the rubedo to 'an increase of warmth and light coming from the sun, consciousness' and to the Sol-Luna marriage; nothing links it to a shadow or dark half of totality — the object inverts the paragraph's sense.
'The oldest traces of it can be found in the Turba, where salt-water and sea-water are synonyms for the aqua permanens' — reported doctrine correctly typed with the Turba named.
'For this reason the experience of the self is always a defeat for the ego' — Jung's own assertion; direction correct.

The text says Maier was 'fully justified in giving the name Isis to the prima materia' — a naming/designation of the feminine transformative substance, which Jung endorses; 'identical-to' overreaches what is a symbolic designation.

'He who held them was like unto the Son of man, in agreement with the puellus regius in the Introitus' — an explicit parallel between the Son of Man figure and the king's son, honestly typed as a reported parallel.

'She is duplex and mutable like Mercurius, and is like him a mediator; hence their identification in alchemy' — Jung asserts the grounds and the identification in his own voice; 'identified-with' (not identical-to) matches the text.
'Stone is the essence of everything solid and earthly. It represents feminine matter' — the lapis symbol represents matter, direction correct, Jung's own voice.

'For Paracelsus sulphur, together with Sal (salt), is the begetter of Mercurius' — salt is a joint begetter of Mercurius per the named source Paracelsus; edge holds, though sulphur is the co-begetter.
'The primary pair of opposites, consciousness and unconsciousness, whose symbols are Sol and Luna' — Luna is the symbol/psychic analogue of the unconscious, direction correct.
